# Andhakaraṇa Sutta (Iti 87 (It 3.38 PTS It 82))

**ID:** Iti 87 (It 3.38 PTS It 82)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)

**Title (Pali):** Andhakaraṇa Sutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Destroyers of Sight

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Andhakaraṇa Sutta* ("Destroyers of Sight", Iti 87; PTS It 82) is a discourse found in the *Itivuttaka* concerning mental cultivation and discernment [SuttaCentral; Windisch 1889]. In this sutta, the Buddha contrasts three types of unskillful thinking (*akusalavitakkā*) with three types of skillful thinking (*kusalavitakkā*) [SuttaCentral; Windisch 1889]. The three unskillful thoughts—sensual thinking (*kāmavitakka*), ill-will thinking (*vyāpādavitakka*), and cruel or harmful thinking (*vihiṃsāvitakka*)—are described by a stock formula as sight-destroying (*andhakaraṇa*), causing lack of vision (*acakkhukaraṇa*), producing ignorance (*aññāṇakaraṇa*), obstructing wisdom (*paññānirodhika*), conducive to vexation (*vighātapakkhika*), and not leading to Nibbāna (*anibbānasamvattanika*) [Windisch 1889]. Conversely, their opposites—beginning with thoughts of renunciation (*nekkhammavitakka*)—are sight-producers (*cakkhukaraṇa*), promote knowledge and wisdom, and lead directly to Nibbāna [Windisch 1889].

SuttaCentral records passage-level parallels in multiple recensions of the *Udānavarga* (UV 12, UVS 12, and Tibetan Uv Kg 12 *Mārgavarga*) and Chinese versions (T 210.28, T 212.13, and T 213.12), as well as resembling parallels in the *Nīvaraṇa Sutta* (SN 46.40) and its Chinese counterpart SĀ 706 [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus similarly finds heavy Pali-internal reuse between this discourse and the *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (specifically SN 46.40, which applies the identical descriptive formula to the five hindrances), the *Dvedhāvitakka Sutta* (MN 19) regarding the division of thoughts, the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 16), the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 2.10), and related *Itivuttaka* discourses (such as Iti 80 and Iti 88) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with the Tibetan *Abhiniṣkramaṇa-sūtra* (D0301) and Chinese T 150A [DharmaNexus].
